pixel_convention: x right, y down, origin top-left, full-resolution pixels

camera.evidence: phase correlation of bottom band and left strip vs frame 0: |shift| < 0.07 px for all sampled frames; background pixels identical up to compression noise

objects.name: phoenix
objects.description: the only moving object: a fantasy bird (phoenix) with green body/neck, green-purple-pink flapping wings and a long red/pink tail with eye-spot (peacock-like) feathers ending in a golden flame-like tip; seen in side view, head pointing LEFT
objects.motion: flies leftward across the frame (head x 1404 -> 158 px) at nearly constant height (head y 663-687 px), flapping wings; leftward speed increases over the clip

extents_px.note: bbox_w is the full body length incl. tail (main axis is horizontal); bbox_h is the vertical wing extent; side view so true wingspan (into the depth) is not visible

objects.reference_point_recommendation: head_x/head_y (leftmost mask pixel = beak tip) is the steadiest body-fixed point; cx_green/cy_green (green body pixels) is near the body/pelvis but jitters with wing pose; cx_mask/cy_mask (whole-mask centroid) swings strongly with the wings and tail. The Blender rig origin is not visible; it is presumably on the body, which translates like the head.

objects.name: sky_background
objects.description: static backdrop: pink/peach sunset sky with a large grey cloud bank across the upper-left/centre (about x 200-1900, y 100-700) and a smaller pink cloud right of centre (about x 1950-2350, y 500-750). No ground, no horizon line, no other objects.

events.event: frames 0 and 1 are (nearly) identical: motion starts after frame 1
wing-beat: bbox_h minima (wings passing horizontal / mid-stroke)
wing-beat period approx 12.4 frames = 0.52 s (about 1.9 beats/s), about 5.7 beats in clip
bird still in frame at last frame (71); never leaves or is occluded

perspective: 2D scene: flight is in a plane facing the camera; the bird's apparent size (bbox_w 550-634, no trend) does not change with time, so one metres-per-pixel scale applies.
